skill.name: auth-tool-cloudbase
skill.description: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CloudBase authentication provider readiness, login method setup, publishable keys, and provider boundaries before implementation.
skill.summary: Prepare CloudBase auth providers and keys before building login flows.
skill.author: tencentcloudbase

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, relative documentation links, and documented OAuth or console URLs. The confirmed risks are the skill's legitimate ability to guide email sender setup, API key lifecycle operations, and privileged auth provider changes that require explicit user approval.

remediation.issue: Provider and API key lifecycle actions can change production authentication state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before add, update, delete, create, or revoke actions, and prefer read-only checks by default.

remediation.issue: SMTP, OAuth, and provider secrets may be handled in prompts or logs.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to provide secrets through secure tool inputs or consoles, avoid echoing secrets, and redact secrets in summaries.

remediation.issue: Markdown code examples triggered many shell execution false positives.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that code blocks are illustrative API payloads and not commands to execute in the local shell.

content.value_statement: Authentication projects fail when providers, login methods, and publishable keys are not ready. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CloudBase auth readiness before implementation starts.
actual_capabilities: Checks CloudBase login configuration before auth implementation.
Guides enabling or disabling username, SMS, email, and anonymous login methods.
Explains provider setup boundaries for WeChat, Google, SMTP email, and OAuth flows.
Directs publishable key lookup and creation for frontend readiness.
Separates management-side auth tools from application-side auth configuration tools.
Routes users to Web, mini program, Node, or HTTP auth implementation guidance after readiness checks.
limitations: It does not implement frontend login screens or backend session logic.
It depends on CloudBase MCP tools or CloudBase APIs being available in the environment.
It cannot verify third-party provider credentials without user access to those provider consoles.
Provider and API key changes can affect production authentication and should require user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Prepare Web Login
use_cases.description: Confirm enabled login methods and publishable key availability before building a CloudBase Web auth flow.

use_cases.title: Configure Provider Readiness
use_cases.description: Review SMS, email, WeChat, Google, and anonymous provider settings before allowing client authentication.

use_cases.title: Audit Auth Setup Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether a task should modify provider settings, client settings, API keys, or implementation code.

prompt_templates.title: Check Login Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to check the current CloudBase login configuration for my selected environment. Tell me which login methods are enabled and what must be configured before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Enable Email Login
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to guide CloudBase email login setup. Confirm the login method, explain the email provider configuration, and ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare OAuth Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare Google or WeChat login for CloudBase. Identify the redirect URL, required provider credentials, and the safe update sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Review Auth Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my CloudBase auth plan across Web, mini program, Node, and HTTP clients. Separate provider setup tasks from implementation tasks and flag risky changes.

output_examples.input: I need email and password login for a CloudBase Web app.
output_examples.output: The skill would report whether email login is enabled, whether the email provider needs sender configuration, and whether the publishable key is ready before UI work starts.

output_examples.input: I want to add Google login to an existing CloudBase app.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify the static domain for the redirect URL, list the required Google credentials, and recommend confirming provider changes before updating CloudBase.

output_examples.input: My app cannot find a publishable key.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide a lookup for the existing publishable key, explain when creation is appropriate, and warn before creating or deleting API keys.

best_practices: Confirm the canonical CloudBase environment ID before generating configuration or console links.
Ask for explicit approval before enabling providers, changing SMTP settings, or creating keys.
Move to the platform-specific implementation skill only after provider readiness is confirmed.
anti_patterns: Do not build login UI before the required CloudBase provider is enabled.
Do not route application-side provider configuration through management-side login tools.
Do not create or delete API keys when a read-only readiness check is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill implement login flows?
faq.answer: No. It prepares provider and key configuration before a platform-specific auth implementation starts.

faq.question: Which tools does it prefer?
faq.answer: It prefers queryAppAuth and manageAppAuth for application-side auth configuration when those tools are available.

faq.question: Can it enable anonymous login?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill states that anonymous login is disabled by default and should only be enabled with explicit need.

faq.question: Does it handle OAuth providers?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WeChat and Google provider readiness, including redirect URL and credential requirements.

faq.question: Can it manage publishable keys?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides lookup and creation of publishable keys, and it warns that key lifecycle actions are sensitive.

faq.question: Is this safe for production environments?
faq.answer: Use caution. Provider, SMTP, and API key changes can affect production authentication and should require confirmation.
